newsitem.title: USA: US official says Japan trade frictions could rise.
newsitem.headline: US official says Japan trade frictions could rise.

text.p: A U.S. trade official said Friday that trade frictions with Japan could rise if a trend suggesting a big increase in Japan's current account surplus continued.

"If the trend continues, we could see a renewal of trade frictions and we want to avoid that, as do the Japanese," the official told reporters in a telephone news conference following release of a U.S. report on auto trade with Japan.

The official said that U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky will meet Japanese International Trade and Industry Minister Shinji Sato in Washington on April 28 to discuss U.S. trade concerns. She will talk about the need for more deregulation and an effort to boost domestic demand in Japan, he said.

The official said that although 1996 looked "pretty good" as far as the car trade report was concerned, the United States was worried that the pace of deregulation called for by a 1995 auto trade agreement has slowed down.
He also said competitive U.S. exporters continue to experience problems getting products through Japan's regulated distribution systems.

He said it was still profitable to sell U.S. cars in Japan despite a stronger dollar and weaker yen and expressed dismay that U.S. car makers have been unable to sign up more than 114 new dealers since the car trade accord was signed last August.
He said the U.S. manufacturers reported that dealers were under pressure from Japan's major carmakers not to sell U.S.-made cars.
A big increase in Japan's trade surplus is bound to attract attention from the media and members of Congress and lead to greater tensions between the United States and Japan, the official said.
